rubric.why: These are the first four taxonomic ranks in the listed sequence.
rubric.description: Names kingdom, phylum, class and order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all four ranks are named in the answer, in any order.

rubric.why: These complete the seven ranks in the Linnaean system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if all three ranks are named.

modelAnswer: In this system, Linnaeus suggested seven taxonomic ranks i.e., kingdom, phylum (division), class, order, family, genus and species.

rubric.why: Archaea have a cell-wall composition that distinguishes them from bacteria.
rubric.description: States that archaeal cell walls lack peptidoglycan and are made of polypeptides or proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the archaeal cell-wall distinction.

rubric.why: The answer distinguishes the groups by comparing their ribosomal RNA.
rubric.description: States that archaeal rRNA resembles eukaryotic rRNA more than bacterial rRNA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the rRNA resemblance to eukaryotes.

modelAnswer: Their cell wall does not contain peptidoglycan but is made of various polypeptides and proteins. Their rRNA (ribosomal RNA) resembles more to eukaryotes than to bacteria. The cell wall is made of peptidoglycan.

rubric.why: The three-kingdom system placed fungi within Plantae.
rubric.description: Identifies that fungi were included in kingdom Plantae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungi were classified in Plantae.

rubric.why: Fungal traits differ from plants and expose the problem with that placement.
rubric.description: Gives a distinguishing fungal trait, such as heterotrophic absorption or a chitin cell wall rather than a cellulose one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant difference between fungi and plants.

modelAnswer: In this system, fungi were still included in the kingdom Plantae. Some taxonomists disagreed about the position of fungi in kingdom Plantae. Fungi resemble plants in many ways but are heterotrophs which get their food by absorption. They do not have cellulose in their cell walls but possess chitin.

rubric.why: The kingdom described is the animal kingdom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Animalia or animals.

rubric.why: These are key characteristics given for organisms in this kingdom.
rubric.description: States that animals are multicellular and heterotrophic.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if both characteristics are stated.

modelAnswer: This kingdom includes animals which are eukaryotic, multicellular and heterotrophic.

rubric.why: Fungi obtain nutrients by absorption rather than ingesting food.
rubric.description: States that fungi are heterotrophic and absorb nutrients from their surroundings or decaying matter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the heterotrophic, absorptive mode of nutrition.

rubric.why: Being eukaryotic and having a chitin cell wall are distinguishing characteristics of fungi.
rubric.description: States that fungi are eukaryotic and have a cell wall made of chitin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the eukaryotic nature and chitin cell wall.

modelAnswer: They are heterotrophic. Fungi get nutrients in a unique way. They do not ingest food like animals and some protists. They absorb food from decaying matter present in their surroundings. Fungi are eukaryotic and have cell wall around their cells. Their cell wall is made of chitin (a polysaccharide).

rubric.why: Archaea and Bacteria are two of the three domains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark if both domains are named.

rubric.why: Eukarya is the remaining domain in the classification.
rubric.description: Names Eukarya as the third domain.

modelAnswer: Living organisms are broadly classified into three domains: Archaea, Bacteria, and Eukarya.

rubric.why: Viruses are excluded from the kingdom classification system.
rubric.description: States that viruses are not included or classified in any kingdom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that viruses are not included in the classification system.

rubric.why: Their exclusion is explained by their lack of the characteristics of the domains of life.
rubric.description: Explains that viruses lack the characteristics of the three domains of life.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving this reason.

modelAnswer: Viruses are not included in the classification system because they lack any of the characteristics of the three domains of life.

rubric.why: A shared scientific name gives organisms the same name across places.
rubric.description: States that an organism's scientific name is the same worldwide.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the scientific name is used consistently around the world.

rubric.why: Standard naming allows biologists speaking different languages to communicate clearly.
rubric.description: States that binomial nomenclature provides a standard means of communication across languages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the standard system to communication across languages.

modelAnswer: The scientific name of an organism is same anywhere in the world. This system provides a standard way of communication, whether the language of a particular biologist is Chinese, Arabic, Spanish, or English.
